source_reviews.independent_solution: Write image coordinates (X,Y,Z). Translation gives X=x-1,Y=y+5,Z=z+3, hence x=X+1,y=Y-5,z=Z-3. Substitution into 3x-y+8z-17=0 gives 3X-Y+8Z-33=0. For the origin homothety k=-3/2, x=X/k,y=Y/k,z=Z/k. Multiplying by nonzero k yields 3X-Y+8Z-17k=0, i.e. 3X-Y+8Z+51/2=0, equivalently 6X-2Y+16Z+51=0. Plane equations are equivalent under any nonzero common multiplier.

Central symmetry about O=(0,0,0): (x,y,z)->(-x,-y,-z), since O is the midpoint. Reflection in z=0: (x,y,z)->(x,y,-z), retaining coordinates parallel to the plane. Symmetry about the z axis (half-turn in space): (x,y,z)->(-x,-y,z), retaining the axial coordinate and reversing both perpendicular ones.

The phrase 'use the preceding exercise' presents the same three transformations in the same order as 35; p0056#9 and #11 explicitly define central symmetry with center O, denoted Z_0. Thus 36(1) means origin central symmetry, without repairing literal lowercase z_0 or deciding O/0 typography. Substituting x=-X,y=-Y,z=-Z into 7x-2y-5z-1=0 gives -7X+2Y+5Z-1=0, equivalently 7X-2Y-5Z+1=0. For z=0 reflection substitute x=X,y=Y,z=-Z: 7X-2Y+5Z-1=0. For z-axis half-turn substitute x=-X,y=-Y,z=Z: -7X+2Y-5Z-1=0, equivalently 7X-2Y+5Z+1=0. All three constants and flipped coordinates are essential.

For general center O, H(P)=O+k(P-O), k nonzero. If k=1 the identity fixes every point, line and plane. If k!=1 the equation H(P)=P forces P=O. A line through O maps onto itself; a plane through O maps onto itself. Conversely a line/plane not through O has a nonzero perpendicular offset from O, multiplied by k; equality of affine sets would require (k-1) times that offset to vanish, impossible. For arbitrary distinct A,B, |H(A)H(B)|=|k||AB|. Thus it is a displacement/isometry exactly when |k|=1: k=1 or k=-1, not just selected examples. k=-1 is central symmetry and qualifies under distance-preserving space displacement.

For each vertex V in {A,B,C,D}, construct V'=O+k(V-O). With k=-2 use the opposite ray from O to V and length OV'=2OV; with k=1/2 use the same ray and half the distance. If a vertex equals O it stays O. Join the six corresponding pairs of image vertices, retaining tetrahedron incidences; negative k is a central reversal, not four independent arbitrary placements. Every face's lengths scale by |k|, its area by k^2, so the whole surface area S'=k^2 S. Required original:image ratios S:S' are 1:4 for -2 and 4:1 for 1/2. Length or volume ratios are not answers.

Choose the specified vertex O as center. O'=O. For each of the other seven vertices V, place V' on OV with OV'=OV/3, then join the twelve corresponding edges and six faces. Equivalently divide each of the three independent edges from O by 3 and use parallels to complete the parallelepiped; images of vector sums are the sums of the image edge vectors. This works for a general oblique parallelepiped, without assuming a rectangular solid. Surface area scales by (1/3)^2=1/9, so original:image is 9:1.
